title: Open Glass Work on One Vehicle — Auto Glass Services
content:
This desk rule of Crestline Collision & Glass governs how much open glass work one vehicle may carry under **Auto Glass Services**, and how glass damage relates to an insurance claim repair order already open on the same vehicle.

## The rule

> A vehicle may have at most the tier's figure for open glass jobs per vehicle, where open means scheduled, in progress or installed; further glass damage on the same vehicle is added to that job. Glass broken in the same loss as an open insurance claim repair is repaired as part of that repair order, never as a separate glass job. The vehicle has no open glass job and no open insurance claim repair order under the same insurer claim number. A glass claim under its own glass claim number is unaffected by a collision repair on another claim.

Scheduled, in progress and installed are statuses of the glass job. The figure for open glass jobs per vehicle is the one set for the job's Auto Glass Services tier.

## Condition for scheduling a glass job

A glass job is scheduled for a vehicle only where **the vehicle has no open glass job and no open insurance claim repair order under the same insurer claim number**. This is judged on the company's system records before the job is scheduled — the vehicle's glass jobs and their statuses, and the vehicle's insurance claim repair orders with their insurer claim numbers and statuses — not on the customer's account of them.

## What counts as the same object

| Record | Matched to the new glass job by | Counts against it when |
|---|---|---|
| Another glass job | the same vehicle | its status is scheduled, in progress or installed |
| An insurance claim repair order | the same vehicle **and** the same insurer claim number | the repair order is open |

A glass job whose status is completed, cancelled, missed or not repairable is not open. An insurance claim repair order on the same vehicle under a different insurer claim number is not matched: a glass claim under its own glass claim number is unaffected by a collision repair on another claim.

## Judgement table

| Open glass job on the vehicle | Open insurance claim repair order on the vehicle under the same insurer claim number | Result under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| No | No | the condition holds; nothing in this rule stands in the way of scheduling |
| Yes | — | no separate glass job; the further glass damage is added to the open job |
| — | Yes | no separate glass job; glass broken in the same loss is repaired as part of that repair order |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A sedan has a Windshield Replacement job in installed status when the owner reports a cracked door glass. The job is still open (installed counts as open), so the door glass damage is added to that job rather than scheduled as a second glass job.
2. A pickup is in the shop on an open insurance claim repair order under claim number A; a rear glass broke in a separate incident and the insurer opened glass claim number B. The repair order is under a different claim number, so it does not stand in the way of a glass job under claim B.
3. A coupe's last glass job was cancelled. A cancelled job is not open, so it does not count against a new glass job on the coupe.
